source.title: Grokking Beyond the Euclidean Norm of Model Parameters
source.citation: Pascal Junior Tikeng Notsawo et al., 2025
source.authors: Pascal Junior Tikeng Notsawo; Guillaume Dumas; Guillaume Rabusseau

record.file_problem: none noted; the full paper and appendix are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports grokking-like delayed generalization using regularizers other than weight decay and in other settings, testing related grokking claims with different interventions and measures.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the study's own reported training/test or training/recovery outcomes, norm trajectories, and data/depth effects. The paper also discusses prior work on circuits, progress measures, and artifacts; those cited results are not recorded as rows. Hyperparameter values shown only in plots are not transcribed as numerical outcomes.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own runs showing delayed generalization on modular addition (MLP, ℓ1/ℓ2/ℓ∗), on non-algorithmic teacher-student and MNIST data, and in linear sparse-recovery and matrix-completion problems. It uses regularizers other than weight decay and different optimizers, so the results bear on V1, V3, V5 and, through the deterministic plain-GD runs, V7.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The paper also proves that the generalization delay scales as 1/(αβ) for a general regularizer. It shows that in shallow sparse and low-rank problems, ℓ2 weight decay with large initialization produces only 'grokking without understanding'. It also argues that deterministic optimization still groks, contradicting stochasticity explanations.
record.recipe_differences: Uses modular addition but replaces or supplements the original weight-decay setup with ℓ1, nuclear-norm, and domain-specific regularization; also studies sparse recovery, matrix completion, teacher-student models, and MNIST.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported delay changes with αβ; larger αβ is reported to shorten it. Data selection/coherence and model depth also change generalization timing and outcome. In the algorithmic task, the study varies regularization and learning rate, not training-set size.

fits_no_version.finding: In deep diagonal linear networks without explicit regularization, depth L=2 gives a tiny delay and L>2 removes it, with staircase-like abrupt transitions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Over-parameterization by depth acts as an implicit sparsity bias that can shorten or remove the grokking delay.

fits_no_version.finding: Selecting high-coherence entries in matrix completion reduces the samples and time needed to generalize. In compressed sensing, higher coherence increases the delay.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: With all other hyperparameters fixed, data selection alone can amplify or reduce the grokking delay.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267 (2025)
record.problems: Several key accuracy and error trajectories are reported only in figures, without text-stated numerical values or uncertainty estimates. The modular-addition experiment uses a fixed rtrain = 40%, so it does not establish the training-set-size trend in V1. The paper's regularization experiments do not directly measure circuit efficiency or test a general critical dataset-size prediction.
record.rows_left_out: No additional result-bearing outcomes were omitted; cited findings from other work and plots that only illustrate quantities used for setup or discussion were not entered as rows.

untested.parts: Growth of the delay as the training set shrinks (rtrain fixed at 40%).
Lazy-to-rich transition; text and molecule data; switching via initialization scale in neural networks.
Circuit efficiency comparison; ungrokking when data falls below a critical size.
Softmax floating-point limits; controlled comparison of Adam against SGD in the neural-network experiments.

missing.what: Grokking-like delay with projected subgradient and proximal (ISTA) methods for sparse recovery and matrix sensing.
In compressed sensing, the coherence parameter τ affects the generalization delay and time (higher τ delays generalization).
With large init, a linear-scale plot makes grokking appear while the log-scale plot shows no true generalization.

record.verdict_notes: Appendix H.3 says the neural-network runs use Adam, so the MLP rows cannot bear on V7; only the linear GD runs do. The paper's 'ungrokking' (the delay vanishing with depth) is not V5's ungrokking below a critical dataset size. Neither original source is this study, so verdicts are allowed.

versions.untested_parts: The modular-addition experiment tests delayed generalization after training accuracy improves, but does not test whether the delay grows as the training set shrinks.
The paper does not identify a generalizing circuit or measure its gradual formation, removal of memorizing components, or predictive progress measures.
Tests non-algorithmic teacher-student and MNIST settings with regularization; does not test initialization-scale switching or a lazy-to-rich transition.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic data is tested.

Tests property-specific regularization, sample/data conditions, and some cases where weight decay fails or the ℓ2 norm is not informative. It does not measure circuit efficiency or test a general critical dataset-size prediction as a distinct theory.
Does not identify or compare learned algorithms across runs.
Does not control for adaptive-optimizer instabilities or floating-point/softmax limitations.
